reason: The cited evidence shows that preheating is used to minimize thermal stresses (E4) and that LPBF thermal cycles induce dislocations and segregation (E3), but none of the passages address AlCrFeNiSi, the specific 300–500 °C preheating window, or the formation and mechanical role of a nonequilibrium SRO state. The key premises linking preheating to SRO stabilization and property improvement are therefore unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Substrate preheating to 300–500 °C reduces thermal gradients and cooling rates during LPBF
Reduced thermal gradients and cooling rates diminish residual thermal stresses
Moderated solidification conditions promote formation of a beneficial nonequilibrium short-range order (SRO) state
The SRO state aids dislocation accommodation and microstructural homogenization
These microstructural changes improve tensile and fatigue properties in miniature AlCrFeNiSi components
